title: An efficient Hamiltonian-based quantum algorithm for characters of the symmetric group
abstract: Consider a quantum state vector proportional to any given column of the character table of the symmetric group ($S_n$), corresponding to a superposition over the irreps weighted by the character values. It was recently argued that sampling from this state is classically hard under reasonable complexity-theoretic assumptions, while there exists an efficient quantum algorithm for preparing this character state using the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) over $S_n$ [arXiv:2501.12579]. We give an alternative, simpler algorithm to prepare this character state with a sequence of Hamiltonian evolutions, as well as an efficient implementation with reconfigurable qubits that uses only nearest-neighbor gates in 1D. The gate complexity, accounting for Hamiltonian simulation errors, depends on the choice of the column: For fixed target state error, the estimated sufficient total gate count ranges from as few as $O(n)$ gates for the $n$-cycle column, to $\widetilde O(n^{1.75})$ gates near the conjecturally classically hard parameter regime, to provably $\widetilde O(n^{2.5})$ gates in the worst case. In contrast, the QFT subroutine in the prior approach uses $\widetilde O(n^3)$ gates. Our gate count estimates come from leading-order state-dependent Trotter error analysis, and the proven worst-case bound relies on a QSVT-based Hamiltonian simulation method; numerical benchmarks of the Trotter-based protocol suggest that the estimates are conservative. Furthermore, we generalize our protocol to give an explicit algorithm for the quantum character transform (QCT) over $S_n$ using $\widetilde O(n^{2.5})$ gates and $O(n)$ qubits. An application to entanglement entropy of symmetric orbifold conformal field theories is also discussed.
summary: This paper presents an alternative, Hamiltonian-based quantum algorithm to prepare quantum states encoding characters of the symmetric group ($S_n$). It achieves better gate complexity bounds than prior QFT methods, providing an explicit algorithm for the Quantum Character Transform (QCT). This work advances the field by offering concrete, resource-aware quantum implementations for mathematically complex quantum states.
main_problem: Developing efficient quantum algorithms to prepare quantum states whose amplitudes encode the characters of the symmetric group ($S_n$).
main_result: The authors propose a Hamiltonian-based approach achieving gate complexities up to $\widetilde O(n^{2.5})$ for the full Quantum Character Transform (QCT), improving upon prior QFT-based estimates of $\widetilde O(n^3)$.
method: The state preparation is achieved by simulating the evolution governed by a specific Hamiltonian ($H_s$) using Trotterization or Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT).
model_or_system: The system is based on the symmetric group $S_n$, utilizing fermionic operators and current operators ($J_s$) acting on a product state to encode character table columns.

(b) One Trotterized transfer on reconfigurable qubits: after the regrouping Ps, the 2n −s bond terms are nearest-neighbor, and the ancilla is swapped along the chain so that each bond gate acts on three adjacent qubits. (c) Block encoding of Hs: V puts the register |i, β⟩in uniform superposition over the Pauli-string labels, and site k receives the Pauli σk ∈{I, X, Y, Z} the register selects: X or Y at i and i + s, Z in between, I elsewhere.

Figure 2: The encoding (2.10) for λ = (3, 1) at n = 4. The boundary of the Young diagram inside the 4×4 box is traced from the bottom left corner to the top right corner. Each step up is recorded as a 1 and each step to the right as a 0, giving a bit string of length 2n and Hamming weight n. The ones sit at the modes λj + n −j + 1, here {1, 2, 4, 7} after padding λ to (3, 1, 0, 0). The empty partition gives |seed⟩= |1n0n⟩.

Figure 3: Chain decomposition (4.1) of the current operator Js, shown for 2n = 10 and s = 3. On the full chain Js hops each mode to the one s sites to its right. Grouping modes by residue class modulo s splits Js into s independent chains J(µ) s , here the residue classes {1, 4, 7, 10}, {2, 5, 8} and {3, 6, 9}, each a nearest-neighbor hopping chain of length Lµ ≈2n/s. The figure shows the decomposition at the level of mode couplings. In the physical ordering, each bond still carries a Jordan–Wigner string over the intervening modes, which the permutation Ps in (4.2) removes.

Figure 4: Circuit for a single bond rotation e−iθhq,a = T † q,a V (θ) Tq,a on the ancilla a and two site qubits q, q+1. The compression Tq,a of (4.7) maps the active subspace onto span{|000⟩, |010⟩}, where V (θ) performs the rotation (4.8), after which T † q,a uncomputes.
